sections.title: How long has this been going on?
sections.content: *óta* ("since") follows a starting point to say how long something has been true: *január* *óta* ("since January"), *gyerekkora* *óta* ("since his/her childhood"; *gyerekkora* is *gyerekkor* with the 3rd-person ending *-a* you know). For a number of years there is no *óta*: *két* *éve* ("it is two years since") does the job, so *két* *éve* *futok* means "I have been running for two years".

items.english: I've been running for two years.
He's been playing football since childhood.

sections.content: Notice futok is present tense, not a past form. Hungarian describes something that started before and is STILL true right now with the present tense plus *óta* or *éve* — English needs "have been running", Hungarian just needs futok.
